name: Create event
what: Starts a draft event: address, title, organiser name/org/contact, purpose, dates, time zone, expected participants.

name: Check address availability
what: Checks whether an event slug (its .simple-hack.app address) is free as the organiser types it.

name: Edit organiser details
what: Updates organiser name, organisation, contact email, purpose and expected participant count.

name: Edit event page text
what: Edits title, tagline, about, rules, prizes and the organiser's own code-of-conduct text (appended to the default, not replacing it).
stages: any (text stays editable after the event ends)

name: Set event dates and time zone
what: Sets the start/end date shown on the page and the IANA time zone every deadline and schedule time is shown in.

name: Set event colour
what: Picks an accent ink colour for the event page, or leaves it automatic (derived from the address).

name: Set event page style
what: Picks a whole-page theme (Poster, Confetti, Boardroom, Garden or Terminal) for the public event page, or Classic for today's look; colour still drives buttons, links and the theme's own highlights.
today_location: Manage > Event page > Look > Page style

name: Upload event icon
what: Uploads a round icon (PNG/JPEG/WebP, up to 128 KB) shown on the event page, directory and join links.

name: Remove event icon
what: Clears the uploaded icon, reverting to an auto-generated initial-letter icon.

name: Switch built-in vs custom website
what: Switches the event's own address between the built-in event page and an uploaded custom site; switching back to built-in keeps the custom files for later.

name: Upload a custom event website
what: Uploads a zip (index.html at root) to replace the event's own page; first publish auto-switches the mode to custom.
today_location: Manage > Event page > Upload a zip

name: View website upload history
what: Shows previously published versions of the event's custom website.
today_location: Manage > Event page > Website on your event address

name: Event website's own saved data
what: The KV/SQLite/file backend behind a custom event website (same mechanism as any Simple Host site), reachable only via API/AI app, not a dedicated manage panel.
stages: any (read always; writes blocked once archived)

name: Event website notifications
what: Subscribes to receive signed messages when visitors save data or upload files through the event's own custom website.

name: Add sponsor
what: Adds a sponsor with name, tier, optional link and an optional logo (PNG/JPEG/WebP up to 128 KB).

name: Reorder or remove sponsors/FAQ/schedule rows
what: Moves a sponsor, FAQ or schedule row up/down or removes it before saving content.

name: Add FAQ item
what: Adds a question/answer pair shown as an accordion on the public event page.

name: Add schedule item
what: Adds a timed item (title, details, start/end) in the event's time zone, optionally with a next step to ask for when it starts. The public and signed-in pages mark the current one "Now" and the next one "Next".

name: Real deadlines in the schedule
what: The event's start and end, the entry deadline (a team's own extension in its own view), the voting window and the time results were published show in the schedule as fixed rows. They come from the settings each time, so they can't drift, and each one says where it is set (Basics, Entries or Results).
today_location: Event page > Schedule, participant Schedule, the public event page

name: A schedule row asks for the next step
what: A schedule row can line up with a forward move (Open sign-up, Start building, Close entries, Start judging, Finish judging, Publish results). When its time comes, Overview's next step asks, e.g. "Kickoff is now. Open sign-up?". The entry deadline does this on its own. It only asks. The stage never moves by itself.
today_location: Event page > Schedule > Add time, Overview > Your next step

name: Starting soon and on now
what: Home and Schedule show one line when a row starts within 15 minutes or is on now ("Demos starts in 12 minutes", "Build time is on now"), counting down while the page is open. In the app only, no email.

name: Read schedule and announcements
what: Sees the live schedule (with Now/Next labels and the event's real deadlines as fixed rows) and posted announcements. Announcements use safe server-rendered HTML with links, bold, bullets and call/video cards; the pinned one comes first, including Home’s first two updates. Judges see the pinned update on Overview.
today_location: Event view > Schedule and announcements card

name: Post announcement
what: Posts a title+message to the event page and signed-in members; can also email every participant. Supports labelled http(s) links, bold, bullets, line breaks, call/video cards, server preview and one pinned announcement shown first to participants and judges. Add link takes Label and Address; email includes matching HTML buttons and full addresses in text.

name: Edit announcement
what: Changes an announcement's title or text; editing never sends a new email. Add link and server Preview work in Edit too. Row menu Pin to top / Unpin replaces the single pin without changing the text; pinned rows show a pill and come first.

name: Delete announcement
what: Removes an announcement from the page and signed-in members' feed.

name: Email participants with an announcement
what: A checkbox on the announcement form that, when ticked, also emails every participant; this is the only way an announcement sends mail.

name: Set sign-up questions
what: Writes up to 8 sign-up questions, one per line; a leading * makes a question required. Existing applications keep the questions they already answered.

name: Require approval before joining
what: Toggles whether people who join with the join link need an organiser decision before they can start/join a team or publish. Applications (people without the link) always wait for a decision, whatever this says.

name: Admit everyone waiting
what: When turning approval off, offers to approve every currently-pending join-link sign-up in the same action instead of leaving them pending. Applications are never admitted this way; they stay waiting for a decision.

name: Review application
what: Sees a pending applicant's name, email, how they came (applied or join link), their optional location, age range and gender, and their sign-up question answers.

name: Approve application
what: Approves a pending applicant so they can start/join a team and publish.

name: Reject application
what: Rejects a pending applicant; they stay a member but cannot start/join a team or publish. Only a still-pending application can be decided.

name: See own approval status
what: Sees a pending/rejected banner explaining why team actions are blocked until an organiser decides.

name: Download participants CSV
what: Exports every approved participant as CSV: name, email, team, team_slug, joined_at, coc_accepted_at, then city, country, age_range, gender, joined_via.

name: Preview join link
what: Shows event details, the code of conduct and sign-up questions before the person decides to join.

name: Join event
what: Agrees to the code of conduct, gives a name, answers sign-up questions and joins as a participant.

name: Check whether an event takes applications
what: Reads whether a listed or public event takes applications right now and what the form asks. Signed out it returns only the event basics and applications_open; signed in it adds the organiser's sign-up questions, the code of conduct, the fixed field choices and the person's own status if they already applied or joined.
stages: any (applications_open is true only in open and building, switch on, not taken down)

name: Apply to join an event
what: For people without a join link. Signs in, gives a name, optionally city and country, age range (Under 18, 18-24, 25-34, 35+) and gender (with Prefer not to say), answers the event's sign-up questions, accepts the code of conduct and becomes a pending participant. Every application waits for an organiser, even on events where join-link sign-ups need no approval.
stages: open, building (applications switch on, event not taken down)
today_location: new: Apply on Find a hackathon rows and on the public event page, form at /e/{slug}/apply

name: Turn applications on or off
what: One switch, on by default for every event: whether people without the join link can apply from Find a hackathon (listed events) and the event's public page. Off hides the Apply button and refuses new applications; ones already waiting stay. The join link is not affected.

name: See applicant details
what: Each waiting application shows the person's email, whether they applied or joined with the link, city and country, age range (Under 18 highlighted) and gender, next to their answers. Unshared fields are left out, not shown as blanks.

name: Filter and sort waiting applications
what: Filters the waiting list by how they came (applied or join link), age range and country, and sorts oldest or newest first. Client-side over the same list; an AI app filters the tool result itself.
today_location: new: Manage > People > Applications filter row

name: Applicant fields in the participants CSV
what: The participants CSV gains five columns at the end: city, country, age_range, gender and joined_via (join link or application). Existing columns keep their order.
today_location: Manage > Results > Export > Download participants CSV

name: Preview judge link
what: Shows event details and code of conduct before accepting the judge invite.

name: Join as judge
what: Agrees to the code of conduct, gives a name and joins as a judge.

name: Preview co-organiser invite
what: Shows what an organiser-invite link grants before accepting.
stages: blocked once archived or taken down

name: Accept co-organiser invite
what: Agrees to the code of conduct and joins as a co-organiser.
stages: blocked once archived or taken down

name: Create co-organiser invite
what: Generates a link anyone can accept until it is revoked or expires in 7 days; creating a new one replaces the previous link.

name: Revoke co-organiser invite
what: Stops the current co-organiser invite link working; people who already accepted stay organisers.

name: Remove co-organiser
what: Removes a co-organiser's manage access; the event's original creator cannot be removed.

name: List and filter people
what: Lists every member with role, approval status, team and join date; filterable by role.

name: Remove person
what: Removes a participant or judge from the event (and their team, if any); they can rejoin with the same join link unless it is regenerated, or apply again while applications are on (that application waits for a decision). Someone who left on their own is no longer in People, and a judge who left keeps a row on Judging instead.

name: Turn off someone's publishing key
what: Revokes another member's personal API key for publishing; they must create a new one themselves.

name: List teams
what: Shows every team with members, admins, track, size and whether it's locked, plus everyone not yet on a team.

name: Rename team
what: Changes a team's display name; its address and join code stay the same.

name: Move member to another team
what: Moves a person onto a team (from another team or none). Works on a locked team, never on a team kept after everyone left.
today_location: Teams > Team detail (Add someone, Move to another team), Teams > Not on a team (Put on a team)

name: Take a member off a team
what: Removes one member from a team; the team gets a new join code.

name: Delete team
what: Removes an entire team, its entry and its site; members become unteamed.

name: Set max team size
what: Sets the most people allowed on one team (1 to 50, 20 by default).

name: Download teams CSV
what: Exports every team and its roster as CSV.

name: Give one team more time
what: Sets a per-team deadline later than the event's own, so a single team can keep building after everyone else is frozen; the event must already have a deadline.
today_location: Manage > Entries tab > Give more time

name: Clear a team's extension
what: Removes a team's deadline extension, reverting it to the event's general deadline.

name: Turn team finding on or off
what: Turns team finding on or off. Off hides Ask to join, Find people and the looking list and refuses requests and invites. Team links and codes, admins, locking and Fill teams work either way.

name: Preview fill teams
what: Plans placing approved people without a team: teams that aren't locked are topped up to the chosen People per team (default 4, at most the team size), then new teams of that size start. Changes nothing yet.
today_location: Teams > Not on a team > Fill teams

name: Apply fill teams
what: Commits the previewed plan, moving people onto teams; the plan uses membership as of the moment it is applied, which may have shifted since the preview.
today_location: Teams > Not on a team > Fill teams (Place N people)

name: View team-finding board
what: Read-only view of open teams and solo people looking for a team, for the organiser's awareness.

name: Browse teams to ask
what: Shows every team that isn't locked or past its deadline, with roster, size, track and its Looking for note. Full teams show as Full.
today_location: Team (no team) > Ask to join a team

name: List self as looking for a team
what: Lists a person without a team as looking, with a one-line intro (up to 120 characters), visible to teams.
today_location: Team (no team) > Ask to join > Let teams find you

name: Ask to join a team
what: Sends a request to join a team that isn't locked. The team's admins say yes or no. Joins immediately if that team already invited you.
today_location: Team (no team) > Ask to join a team

name: Withdraw a join request
what: Cancels your own pending request to join a team.
today_location: Team (no team) > Ask to join a team

name: Invite a solo participant
what: Any team member invites a person who is looking for a team. Joins immediately if that person already asked. Refused while the team is locked.

name: Cancel a sent invite
what: Cancels an invite your team sent to a solo person.

name: Accept request or invite
what: A team admin accepts an incoming join request, or the invited person accepts their own invite. Joining clears every other pending offer for that person. Refused while the team is locked or full.
today_location: Team > Members (requests) / Team (no team) > Invites for you

name: Decline request or invite
what: A team admin declines an incoming join request, or the invited person declines their invite.
today_location: Team > Members (requests) / Team (no team) > Invites for you

name: Remove a team member
what: A team admin removes another member, admins included, never themselves. The team link changes and the removed person sees a notice.

name: See team-removal notice
what: Shows a notice explaining that you were taken off a team, on Home and on Team, when you have no current team.

name: Needs you
what: Shows a Needs you card above the next-step card on Home, one row per thing waiting on this person -- join requests and invites for their team, a request or application answered, a team or site change, a new admin -- each row linking to its own screen, with a Dismiss button on news rows.
today_location: new: Participant Home > Needs you card

name: Applications waiting
what: Shows a Needs you line on Overview when applications are waiting for a decision, a count with a Review applications link to People, matching the People sidebar badge.
today_location: new: Organiser Overview > Needs you line

name: Needs you across events
what: Shows a Needs you card on Home listing everything waiting on this person across every event they belong to, each row named for its event and linking into it; an AI app reads the same list across every event in one call.

name: Dismiss a notice
what: Dismisses one news line (a request answered, a site or deadline change, a new admin, a team removal) from a Needs you card so it stops showing; it never reappears once dismissed.
today_location: new: Needs you card Dismiss button

name: Email me when something waits on me
what: Toggles whether team requests and invites, application answers, and team or site changes are also emailed, batched to at most one email of each kind every 15 minutes; organisers hear about new applications by count only, never names. Disabled for a key-only account.

name: Announcements unread badge
what: Shows a count on the Announcements sidebar item for announcements posted since this browser last opened the screen; opening Announcements clears it at once, kept in this browser's own storage, not the server. Uses the newest created_at, even when an older pinned announcement is first.

name: Set what teams hand in, line by line
what: Each entry line is Required, Optional or Off; the show-your-work lines (video, website, code link, screenshot) can also be One of, meaning at least one of those must be there. Title is always required. Enforced on Submit, not on draft saves. Replaces the old entry_required list, which keeps working one release as a deprecated alias.
stages: draft, open, building (read-only once entries close)

name: Set submission deadline
what: Sets the date/time (in the event's time zone) after which team sites and entries freeze.
stages: any; cannot move it earlier once entries are already closed/judging/results without first moving the stage back to Building

name: Clear submission deadline
what: Removes the deadline entirely so teams can keep changing sites and entries until a new one is set.

name: Show entries on the event page
what: Toggles whether published team sites appear in a public gallery on the event page; also gates whether voting can be enabled.

name: View entries progress
what: Counts at the top (submitted, drafts, not started, sites live) and each team's status (Submitted, Draft with what's missing, Not started, Not submitted after the deadline), extension and site state.

name: Take a team's site down
what: Hides a team's published site with an optional reason the team can see (e.g. a content violation).

name: Put a team's site back
what: Restores a site the organiser took down; refused if the platform (not the organiser) took it down.

name: Download entries CSV
what: Downloads every entry as CSV: status, submitted_at, the summary card lines, links, has_screenshot, what's missing under the current rules.

name: Download all team sites
what: Downloads every team's published files and saved data as one archive; marked private since it includes previously stored private data.

name: View own entry
what: Reads the team's entry and which fields are still missing for completeness.

name: Edit entry fields
what: Edits title, tagline, description, video link and code link; an empty string clears a field.
stages: building (until the team is frozen or taken down)

name: Resolve a teammate's concurrent edit
what: When a teammate changed the entry since this person opened it, choose to keep your own text or take the newer version (optimistic-concurrency prompt).

name: Upload entry screenshot
what: Uploads a screenshot (PNG/JPEG/WebP, up to 2 MB); saves as soon as the file is chosen.

name: Remove entry screenshot
what: Deletes the uploaded screenshot.

name: View entry read-only
what: Sees the entry exactly as submitted once frozen, taken down or the event has ended.

name: Download own team site archive
what: Downloads the team's own published files and saved data as an archive.
today_location: Team site card > Download our team site

name: Get a publishing key
what: Creates a one-time-shown API key for a coding agent or the command line to publish the team site.

name: Replace publishing key
what: Rotates the team's key; the old one stops working at once.

name: Turn off publishing key
what: Revokes the team's key so nothing can publish with it.

name: Upload team site as a zip
what: Publishes the team's site from a zip with index.html at the root; the server does not run any code, only serves files.

name: Connect an AI app to publish
what: Connects an AI app to the connector to publish the team's site without a key. The Website screen now guides it per app and shows Connected and Published from real data.
today_location: Website > Publish from your AI app

name: View team site status
what: Sees the team's address, whether it is live, still being set up, frozen, or taken down (with the organiser's reason).
today_location: Website, state strip (Website half) and Your team site card

name: Team site notifications
what: Subscribes to receive signed messages when visitors save data or upload files on the team's own site.
mcp: list_notifications, remove_notification (partial: create, pause/resume, test, rotate-secret and deliveries stay website-only)

name: Add tracks/challenges
what: Adds a named track with its own challenge text and prize; teams later pick one.

name: Remove a track
what: Deletes a track; warns how many teams currently have it chosen, who will be left with no track.

name: Choose team track
what: Any team member picks or clears the team's track. Saves on change.

name: Define judging rubric
what: Sets up to 10 criteria, each with a name, optional description, weight (must sum to 100%) and a points scale (1–10).

name: See the rubric
what: Reads the event's judging rubric read-only: each criterion's name, description, weight and max points, never a score. No organiser setting hides it; teams always see the rubric.
today_location: Team > Entry > How you're judged card, linked from Home

name: Confirm score deletion
what: A required extra confirmation step when a rubric change (removing a criterion or lowering its points) would delete existing scores; shows the count first.

name: Reorder rubric criteria
what: Moves a criterion up or down in the rubric before saving.

name: Choose judge assignment mode
what: Picks how judges are matched to teams: open (every judge scores every team), automatic, manual, or panels by track.

name: Set judges per team
what: Sets the target number of judges per team for automatic assignment (1–20).

name: Generate automatic assignments
what: Fairly assigns judges across teams (optionally including organisers), skipping declared conflicts; reports any team that got fewer judges than planned. Replaces the previous automatic assignment set.

name: Manual judge assignment grid
what: Ticks which judge scores which team one by one; conflicted pairs stay excluded.

name: Track panel assignment grid
what: Ticks which judges sit on each track's panel.

name: Warn about teams with no track
what: In panel mode, names every team with no track (they match no panel and get no judges) on the Judging Progress card, on the Overview next-step card before Start judging, and with a count in the Start judging confirm -- each with a link to Teams. Computed client-side from GET .../teams's per-team track and GET .../judging/settings's assignment_mode; no server field needed.
today_location: Manage > Judging > Progress, and Overview's next step before Start judging

name: Declare a judge's conflict
what: Records a conflict of interest between a judge and a team on the judge's behalf, removing that team from the judge's queue.

name: Remove a declared conflict
what: Clears a recorded conflict so that judge can be assigned to that team again.

name: Choose tie-break criterion
what: Picks which rubric criterion is used first to break a tie; this setting locks once judging begins.

name: Choose score mode
what: Picks raw mean or normalised mean as the deciding score for ranking; both are always kept.

name: Show scores publicly
what: Toggles whether numeric scores appear on the public page and results API, independent of showing ranks.

name: Show ranks publicly
what: Toggles whether ranks/tied flags appear on the public page and results API, independent of showing scores.

name: View judging dashboard
what: Shows per-team "N judges scored" and per-judge "done/assigned" counts, flagging teams that fall short of target coverage.

name: Preview current standings
what: Shows the computed ranking right now, without publishing it.

name: Publish results
what: Snapshots the current standing as the official result; teams see it at once, and the public page shows it only if the organiser also chooses to show it. Can be republished later if scores change — later publishes overwrite the snapshot, they do not live-recompute afterwards.

name: Override a tied rank
what: Manually orders teams within a tied group when publishing, overriding the computed tie-break.

name: Choose results visibility
what: Chooses "winners only" (rank 1 and track winners) vs "full ranking" for the public page; only takes effect after results are published.

name: Download scores CSV
what: Exports every judge's per-criterion scores and comments as CSV.

name: Download results CSV
what: Exports computed or published results as CSV.

name: View judging queue
what: Lists entries assigned/eligible to this judge, sorted least-covered-first, with done and conflict state.
stages: closed, judging (scoring is open only in these stages)

name: Preview the entry website while scoring
what: The team's submitted (pinned) version, or the live site before the pin, shows in a framed preview on the scoring screen, with the host named and Open in a new tab. Sites behind a passcode or named viewers can't be framed and show the screenshot with a big Open website button.

name: Score a criterion
what: Taps a point value for one rubric criterion; saves immediately so a flaky connection only ever loses the one tap.

name: Comment on an entry
what: Writes a private comment for the team (not shown with the judge's name); autosaves after a score exists, and on navigation. Cannot be saved before any score exists.

name: Save & next
what: Moves to the next team in the queue after saving the current one's comment; becomes "Save & finish" on the last team.

name: Declare own conflict
what: Flags a conflict of interest with a team, which removes it from the judge's own queue entirely (not just hidden).

name: Remove own conflict
what: Undoes a conflict this judge declared, which puts the team back in their queue.
today_location: AI app (no dedicated web button for judges)

name: View own conflicts
what: Lists the teams this judge has flagged a conflict with; a judge never sees another judge's conflicts or scores.

name: Replay judging walkthrough
what: Reopens the first-time guided tour explaining the queue, scoring and conflicts.

name: Enable people's choice voting
what: Turns on public/participant voting for the event; requires the entry gallery to already be open.

name: Set voting window
what: Sets when voting opens and closes, in the event's time zone.

name: Set voting eligibility
what: Chooses who may vote: anyone signed in, approved event members, or approved participants only; narrowing it can remove existing votes that no longer qualify, which requires an explicit confirmation showing the count.

name: List event in directory
what: Makes the event visible on simple-hack.app's public directory; new events are unlisted by default.

name: Cast or change a vote
what: Picks one team to vote for; a repeat vote silently replaces the previous one, with no additive or undo model. Organisers and accounts with no personal username cannot vote.

name: View final vote ranking
what: Sees vote counts/ranking once voting has closed.

name: View own current vote
what: Sees which team this person currently has voted for, while voting is open.

name: View own team result
what: Sees the team's rank, deciding score (with raw and normalised totals shown), any track-winner note, and judges' comments.
today_location: Results > Your entry as the public sees it

name: View public results page
what: Sees winners-only or full ranking, exactly as the organiser chose, with scores/ranks shown only if those toggles are on.

name: View public event page
what: Reads title, tagline, about/rules/prizes, schedule, sponsors, FAQ, announcements, entry gallery, status and a live countdown to the deadline.

name: Browse public directory
what: Lists listed events grouped as happening now, upcoming and past. A row whose event takes applications right now carries an Apply button; the row title still opens the event page.

name: Open a team site from the gallery
what: Opens a published team site from the public entries gallery on the event page.

name: Change event stage
what: Moves the event between draft → open → building → closed → judging → results → archived. Moving a stage backward shows a confirmation describing the specific effect (e.g. reopening entries, reopening judging); closing entries and archiving each get their own confirmation; entering a submissions-closed stage sets the deadline to now if none has passed yet, and moving back to open/building clears a passed deadline and passed team extensions. Moving to Results locks judging too, when it isn't locked yet.

name: End the event
what: Moves the event to Ended; requires at least one participant (nobody-joined events should be deleted instead); final and cannot be undone.

name: Regenerate join link
what: Issues a new join link/code; the old one stops working at once.

name: Regenerate judge link
what: Issues a new judge link/code; the old one stops working at once.

name: Copy join/judge link
what: Copies the current join or judge link to the clipboard to share.

name: View event stats
what: Shows participants, teams, how many people can judge, and how many are on no team.

name: View storage usage
what: Shows bytes used by the event's team sites on this instance.

name: Delete event
what: Permanently removes the event, its page, results, team sites, entries, scores and votes; a busy or ended event requires typing the exact event address to confirm, an empty never-joined event needs no confirmation body; the address stays reserved afterward unless nobody ever joined. No undo.

name: Leave team
what: Leaves the current team while it is not frozen. If the leaver was the only admin, the longest-standing member becomes admin. The only member leaving deletes the team before its deadline.

name: Start a team
what: Creates a team with a name. The person who starts it is its admin.
stages: open, building (before the deadline for new teams)
today_location: Team (no team) > Start a new team

name: Join team by code
what: Joins a team with its link or code, straight away. A team with its own extension can still be joined after the general deadline. Refused when the team is locked or full.
today_location: Team (no team) > Join with a link or code
mcp: hack_join_team (code may be the whole link)

name: Copy team link
what: Copies the team's link (and shows its code for saying out loud) so teammates can join in one tap. Any member can copy it.
api: n/a (client copy, link from GET /v1/hack/events/{slug} me.team.link)

name: Who am I
what: An AI app checks which account it is signed in as, and which team's site its publishing tools currently act on.
today_location: AI app only, no web screen

name: Edit display name
what: Changes the name shown to teams, organisers and judges.

name: Change email
what: Changes the sign-in email; requires a code sent to both the old and new address, and signs out every other key.

name: Link Google sign-in
what: Links a Google account for faster sign-in to this email.

name: Unlink identity
what: Removes a linked Google/GitHub identity.

name: Toggle sign-in alerts
what: Emails the person after each new sign-in or newly connected app, so an unfamiliar one stands out.

name: Rotate personal API key
what: Issues a fresh personal API key; the previous one stops working.

name: Sign out
what: Signs this browser out: ends its key and the sign-ins it opened, then returns to the landing.
today_location: Sidebar foot (Account, Sign out, Help), on phone in the Menu sheet

name: Sign out everywhere
what: Stops every key, disconnects every connected app, and ends sign-ins on the person's own sites; this browser gets a fresh key.

name: Delete own account
what: Permanently deletes the account and all its data; blocked while organising an event that has not ended. Removed from every event joined; name comes off ended events organised. No undo.

name: Set theme preference
what: Sets system/light/dark theme preference, stored per account (the product itself ships light-only by current design decision).
today_location: Preferences (not surfaced as a visible control in this UI today)

name: Replay organiser walkthrough
what: Reopens the first-time guided tour of the manage dashboard.

name: View as platform admin
what: The Simple Host platform admin can open any event in a read-only pseudo-organiser view (every control disabled except reading, filtering and copying); a banner says so.

name: Replay participant walkthrough
what: Reopens the first-time guided tour of Overview, or of Team while still looking for one, from wherever Help is opened.

name: Replay scoring walkthrough
what: Reopens the first-time guided tour of the scoring page, carrying the team currently open.

name: Leave this event
what: Anyone leaves an event they joined, any time before it ends. A participant leaves their team: before its deadline a lone member's team, entry and site are deleted; past the deadline, or once the event is closed, judging or results, leaving never touches the team, its entry, its site or its scores, even for the last member -- it only takes them off the member list. A judge's scores stay and keep counting. A co-organiser just leaves. The creator hands the event over first, the last organiser ends or deletes it. A preview says what will happen before the confirm. Not on an ended or taken-down event.
today_location: Proposed SIM-388/SIM-393: organiser-settings, participant-home, judge-home, landing-your-events

name: Withdraw an application
what: A participant whose application or join-link sign-up is pending, or was rejected, takes it back. The row and its answers, city, country, age range and gender are deleted. They can apply again while sign-up is open, and the organiser decides again -- no extra machinery stops a second application after a rejection.
stages: any until ended (while pending or rejected)
today_location: new (SIM-340, not built yet): the waiting card's danger zone, Home row … menu

name: Hand the event to another organiser
what: The event creator picks a current co-organiser to become the main organiser (events.created_by) as they leave. Only possible as part of leaving.

name: End or delete the event while leaving as its last organiser
what: The only organiser leaving chooses End the event (page and results stay, nothing can change) or Delete the event (typed address to confirm). End needs at least one participant to have joined.

name: Delete a departed judge's scores
what: Deletes the scores and comments of a judge who left the event, so they stop counting toward totals and ranks. Refused while judging is locked. Published results change only on the next publish.
stages: closed, judging, results (not while locked, not once ended)
today_location: new (SIM-340, not built yet): Judging > Progress > Judges, 'Left the event' row

name: Move the event forward
what: One button on Overview performs the next forward move after a confirm: Open sign-up, Start building, Close entries, Start judging, Finish judging (moves to Results and locks judging), Publish results, End event. The server computes the step as next_step on the organiser's event view.
risk: destructive for End event, reversible otherwise

name: See the event's stage
what: Every role sees the event's stage in the top bar in the same words, and the full stage track on their home screen. Read-only for participants and judges. Judges also see whether scoring is open.
today_location: Status bar on every in-event screen

name: Join a team from its link
what: Opening a team link (/team/{code}) shows the team and joins it after one confirm, for an approved participant with no team. Signed out: sign in first, then back to the link. Never admits anyone to the event itself.
stages: open, building (the team not locked, not full, not past its deadline)

name: Rename the team and set its Looking for note
what: A team admin renames the team (its website address stays the same) and writes the one-line Looking for note shown to people browsing teams.

name: Make or remove a team admin
what: A team admin makes another member admin, or removes admin from one (themselves included) as long as one admin remains. Organisers can do the same from Team detail. When the last admin leaves, the longest-standing member becomes admin automatically.
stages: open, building (not frozen) for admins, any (not ended) for organisers
today_location: Team > Members row menu, Teams > Team detail row menu

name: Lock or unlock a team
what: A team admin (or an organiser) locks the team so no more people can join: requests, link and code joins, invites and Fill teams stop, and pending requests and invites are cleared. Unlocking lets people in again. An organiser can still place someone on a locked team by hand.
stages: open, building (not frozen) for admins, any (not ended) for organisers

name: Make a new team link
what: A team admin (or an organiser) replaces the team's link and code. The old ones stop working at once. Taking someone off a team still does this automatically.
stages: open, building (not frozen) for admins, any (not ended) for organisers

name: Fill in the entry summary card
what: Fixed short lines judges read first: problem (one line, 140), solution (one line, 160, stored as the existing tagline), who it's for (100), track, tools and AI as tags, and what works today. Replaces the free-form summary slide many events ask for.
api: PUT /v1/hack/events/{slug}/entry (problem, tagline, audience, tools, maturity, track)

name: Tag the tools and AI used
what: Up to 10 tags of up to 30 characters, picked from a fixed suggestion list (AI apps, then tools) or typed. Deduplicated without regard to case.

name: Say what works today
what: One of Demo-ready (works end to end), Partly working (some parts are mocked) or Concept (designs or a plan).

name: Choose the track on the entry
what: The entry's Track line is the team's track: changing it on Entry changes the team's track, under the same rule as the Team screen (any member, until the team's deadline).

name: Submit the entry
what: Any team member submits. The server checks the event's rules and refuses with the missing lines (422 entry_incomplete) if anything Required or the One-of rule is not met. Submitted entries are what judges see.

name: Move the entry back to draft
what: Un-submits before the team's deadline, for a team that wants to rework the entry without it counting as finished. A draft that is complete at the deadline is still submitted automatically.

name: Complete drafts submit themselves at the deadline
what: At the team's effective deadline, or when the organiser moves the event to Closed or Judging, a draft that meets every rule is submitted for the team (marked automatic). A draft that does not stays Not submitted and is not judged; the organiser's way in is a per-team extension.
today_location: new (server sweep, same timer as deadline pins)

name: See the card as judges see it
what: A live preview of the summary card beside the form (under it on a phone), with unfilled lines marked, plus the rubric with weights.

name: Follow the entry checklist on Home
what: Four steps ticked from real data: join or start a team, fill in the summary card, show your work (the event's rule, e.g. a video or a website), submit. The first unticked step becomes the Your next step card. The server computes the steps (progress) so the website, AI apps and reminder emails agree.

name: See a live countdown to the team's own deadline
what: Counts down to the team's effective deadline (extension included, and says so). Updates every minute, every second in the last hour; turns amber under 24 hours and red under 1 hour.

name: See whether an AI app is connected and the site published
what: Two states side by side: AI app (Not connected / Connected in <app>, last used, team selected / Connected but another team selected; plus how many teammates are connected, as a count) and Website (Not published / Published, version and time / Taken down). Read from oauth_grants.selected_team_id + oauth_clients.client_name and the team site. The page re-checks every 5 seconds for 10 minutes while waiting.

name: Follow step-by-step setup for an AI app
what: Tabs for Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code and Other AI apps, each with numbered steps taken from the same source as /get-started, the email to sign in with, and ticks that follow the real connection state. Other AI apps links to the matching /get-started section.
today_location: Website > Publish from your AI app (Claude / ChatGPT / Claude Code tabs, steps shared with /get-started)

name: Copy a ready prompt for the AI app
what: A prompt naming the event and team, prefilled with the entry's problem and solution lines when filled, so the AI app knows which team site to publish.
today_location: Website > Publish from your AI app, step with Copy prompt
api: n/a (built in the page from GET /entry)

name: Choose an entry preset
what: SIM-382: exactly two now -- Video or website (default for new events: at least one of a demo video or a website) or Video, website and code link (all three required). Each sets every line's mode and which media judges see first. An event already on a retired preset (AI build, Coding, Ideas and design, Custom) keeps its own lines, shown with neither card selected; setting a retired preset is refused, naming the two current ones. Changing any line afterwards shows the preset as Custom.

name: Choose entry rules before sign-up opens
what: SIM-382: a brand-new event's Overview opens on "Choose what teams hand in" as its first next step, before "Open sign-up" is even offered -- Video or website is already selected. Saving any choice there, even the unchanged default, moves the next step on. An event that already had rules (every event that existed before this shipped) skips it.

name: Choose what judges see after the card
what: Video first or Website first. The summary card is always first.

name: Read the entry summary card first
what: The scoring screen opens on the team's card: name, track, problem, solution, who it's for, tools and AI, what works today. Judges only see submitted entries.

name: Watch the demo video on the scoring screen
what: YouTube, Vimeo, Loom and Google Drive links play in a click-to-load player on the same screen (nothing loads before the tap, no autoplay). Any other host is a large link that names the host.

name: See each criterion's weight while scoring
what: Each criterion shows its share of the total weight (e.g. 40%) beside its name, on the scoring screen and the Home-side rubric.

name: Catch an unscored criterion on Save and next
what: If any criterion has no score, the first press of Save and next shows one line naming it; a second press moves on. No dialog.
today_location: Score screen, one line above Save & next

name: See what each team built in the results
what: Each result the organiser shows (winners only, or the full ranking) carries the team's summary card, website and video link (host named, never embedded) and code link when the event asks for one. Taken from the results snapshot.
today_location: Public event page > Results (cards: winners open, others folded)

name: See tools tags on team site cards after results
what: After results, team site cards for teams shown in the results add their tools tags and link to their result card.
today_location: Public event page > Team sites cards (tags, See result)

name: Get a reminder before an unsubmitted entry closes
what: One email to each member of a team whose entry is not submitted, at each configured Reminder times offset (default 24 hours and 1 hour) before the team's effective deadline, naming what's missing. Uses the existing per-minute event-mail sweep.

name: Password sign-in
what: On a self-hosted install, sign in or create a username/password account; replace a temporary password before entering.
today_location: Shared sign-in card, including /signin and application sign-in

name: Needs you (judge)
what: Shows a Needs you card on judge Overview, above the status line: judging opening and, while teams are still unscored, a reminder before judging closes, each dismissable and linking to My teams.

name: Get reminded before judging closes
what: One email (and the matching in-app news line) to each judge who still has an unscored team in their queue, at each configured Reminder times offset before judging closes.
today_location: Email + Judge Overview Needs you (notices queue, kind judging_reminder)

name: Message a team
what: Sends a short message (up to 1000 characters) to one team, or up to 25 selected teams at once, which reaches every current member in app and by email.
today_location: new: Team > Message team button; Teams > row checkboxes > Message selected

name: Message the organisers
what: Any team member can write to the organisers in the team’s shared thread. Organiser Home shows one unread line per team with Read and reply; opening the thread clears it for that organiser. Emails follow the organiser’s Account preference, at most once per 15 minutes, when mail is set up.
today_location: Team > Members > Messages with the organisers; organiser Home > Needs you; organiser Team > Messages

name: See messages with a team
what: Lists both directions in the team’s thread, newest first. Opening it clears this organiser’s unread Home line. The response includes from_team for each message.

name: See messages with the organisers
what: Shows both directions on Team’s Members tab, newest first, with sender, team or organiser, and relative and absolute times. Empty: No messages yet. After End, hide the card if empty. The response includes from_team for each message.
today_location: Team > Members > Messages with the organisers

name: Set reminder times
what: Sets the list of offsets (up to 5, 15 minutes to 14 days each) that drive both the entry-deadline reminder emails to teams and the judging-closes reminders to judges; shown as removable chips with an add control.

name: Set when judging closes
what: Sets (or clears) judging_ends_at, the plain event time that judging-closes reminders key off; no inference from the schedule.

Below the list, plain details contains Claude / ChatGPT / Claude Code steps with the connector address inside the steps, plus Other AI apps link buttons. Empty or failed loads open Connect an AI app; connections close Connect another app; loading starts closed.
